How it works

A web page in front of iPerf3 and Netperf, with history stored on the router.

Per-WAN tests

Test the active primary WAN, a connected physical WAN, or (manual iPerf3 only) an individual SD-WAN tunnel. Unsupported engine and device combinations are disabled, not silently tried.

Servers

iPerf3 can use the bundled public server catalog, your own saved User Server List, or a one-time Custom Server. Netperf needs no iPerf3 server.

Cellular detail

The app reports what NCOS exposes about the radio. It does not force carrier aggregation or 5G.

Config hierarchy

Each setting area resolves as This Device, then NetCloud Manager Group, then Built-in Default.

See it in the app

SDK Data settings

Only the web port is a field you set. The app manages its own configuration documents, which you edit in the web page.

SettingRequiredDefaultWhat it does
speedtest_analyzer_web_portNoFirst free port from 8000, then savedWeb UI port, 1024 to 65535. If set, the app uses exactly this port. If not set, it uses 8000, or the next free port up to 8100 if 8000 is busy, and saves it here only in that case. A bad value or a busy port stops the app and logs why. Restart the app after changing it.
speedtest_analyzer_groupNoNoneShared configuration for a NetCloud Manager group. The Settings page generates the JSON for you to paste in. The app reads it and does not write to it.
speedtest_analyzer_deviceNoNoneConfiguration for this one router, written by the app when you change a setting in the web page. It takes precedence over the group value for the areas it contains.
  • Set the port in Ericsson NetCloud Manager under the device or group SDK Data.
  • Web page: http://router_ip:<port>, port from the app log. Through NetCloud Manager LAN Manager no firewall change is needed.
  • From the local LAN, the readme says to forward the Primary LAN Zone to the Router Zone and the Router Zone to the Primary LAN Zone.
  • iPerf3 needs a reachable iPerf3 server. Netperf needs access to the native Netperf service. Ookla is optional and needs your own licensed ARM64 binary.
  • NCOS 7.26.x is recommended. Some platforms have disabled engines, listed in the app readme under Known engine limitations. Optional geolocation services in Cellular Analysis need extra keys, described in the readme.
